verdicts.title: On curves with high multiplicity on $\mathbb{P}(a,b,c)$ for $\min(a,b,c)\leq4$
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: On a weighted projective surface $\mathbb{P}(a,b,c)$ with $\min(a,b,c)\leq 4$, we compute lower bounds for the {\em effective threshold} of an ample divisor, in other words, the highest multiplicity a section of the divisor can have at a specified point. We expect that these bounds are close to being sharp. This translates into finding divisor classes on the blowup of $\mathbb{P}(a,b,c)$ that generate a cone contained in, and probably close to, the effective cone.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns effective thresholds of ample divisors on weighted projective surfaces P(a,b,c), with no mention of Del Pezzo degree, regular graphs, or circuit complexity. It shares only generic algebraic-geometry vocabulary and does not interact with the conjecture's specific claim.

verdicts.title: Projective Rigidity of Circle Packings
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We prove that the space of circle packings consistent with a given triangulation on a surface of genus at least two is projectively rigid, so that a packing on a complex projective surface is not deformable within that complex projective structure. More broadly, we show that the space of circle packings is a submanifold within the space of complex projective structures on that surface.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses projective rigidity of circle packings on complex projective surfaces of genus ≥ 2, with no mention of Del Pezzo surfaces, d-regular graphs, or circuit complexity. It shares only loose vocabulary ('projective surface') and does not interact with the conjectured D(G)=Θ(E(G)) correlation.

verdicts.title: On the structure of open del Pezzo surfaces
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Let $(X,D)$ be an open log del Pezzo surface of rank one, that is, $X$ is a normal projective surface of Picard rank one, the boundary $D$ is a reduced nonzero divisor on $X$, and the anti-log canonical divisor $-(K_X+D)$ is ample.
